title: Refining the booking design
idea: Refinement is improving a working design in small steps, with tests passing after each step, and optimising only where a measured cost appears.
points: Refactor first for clarity: remove duplication, sharpen names, shrink long methods.
Measure before optimising; count the work done by code that runs on every booking.
Keep the interface fixed, so `BookingService` and its tests do not change.
Here, indexing by room means each overlap check reads only that room's bookings.

hero.title: Before and after one refinement

left.title: List repository
items: Stores every booking in one array
Each overlap check reads all bookings
Work grows with total bookings in the building

right.title: Indexed repository
items: Stores bookings in a `Map` keyed by room
Each check reads only that room's bookings

hero.verdict: Swap the repository behind its interface; the service never notices.

code.title: Measure, then index
code.caption: Both repositories answer the same question. Compare how many bookings each one reads.

walk.text: A counter records how many bookings each lookup touches.
The list version filters the whole array on every lookup.
The indexed version groups bookings by `roomId` when they are saved.
A lookup reads only one room's list, or an empty one.
Load the same bookings, spread across many rooms, into each repository.
Reset the counter, then measure a single lookup.

pitfalls: Do not optimise code you have not measured; clarity usually matters more.
Run the full test suite after every refactor step, not only at the end.
Keep the index in step with cancellations, or stale bookings will block rooms.

quiz.why: Room `R3` has no entry in the `Map`, so `forRoom` falls back to an empty list and reads nothing.

takeaway: Refine in small, tested steps, and optimise only what you measured.

starters: What other parts of BookingService are worth refactoring?
